True Statement: The chromosomes in the nucleus of a cell contain information for inheritance of features from parents to the next generation in the form of DNA molecules.
False 1: The chromosomes in the cytoplasm of a cell contain information for inheritance of features from parents to the next generation in the form of DNA molecules.

True Statement: DNA in the cell nucleus is the information source for making proteins; if the information is changed, different proteins will be made.
False 1: DNA in the cell nucleus is the information source for making lipids; if the information is changed, different lipids will be made.

True Statement: A basic event in reproduction is the creation of a DNA copy, which creates two copies of DNA in a reproducing cell.
False 1: A basic event in reproduction is the destruction of the original DNA, which creates one copy of DNA in a reproducing cell.

True Statement: DNA copying is accompanied by the creation of an additional cellular apparatus; then the DNA copies separate, each with its own cellular apparatus, effectively dividing the cell into two.
False 1: DNA copying is accompanied by the destruction of the cellular apparatus; then the DNA copies separate, each without any cellular apparatus.

True Statement: The process of copying DNA will have some variations each time because no bio-chemical reaction is absolutely reliable.
False 1: The process of copying DNA is absolutely accurate because bio-chemical reactions are perfectly reliable.

True Statement: The inbuilt tendency for variation during reproduction is the basis for evolution.
False 1: The inbuilt tendency for variation during reproduction is the basis for extinction.

True Statement: Variation is useful for the survival of species over time when environmental conditions change drastically.
False 1: Variation is harmful for the survival of species over time when environmental conditions change drastically.

True Statement: For unicellular organisms, cell division or fission leads to the creation of new individuals.
False 1: For multicellular organisms, cell division or fission leads to the creation of new individuals.

True Statement: In Amoeba, the splitting of the two cells during division can take place in any plane; this is binary fission.
False 1: In Amoeba, the splitting of the two cells during division occurs in a definite orientation; this is binary fission.
False 2: In Leishmania, the splitting of the two cells during division can take place in any plane; this is binary fission.

True Statement: In Leishmania, which has a whip-like structure at one end of the cell, binary fission occurs in a definite orientation.
False 1: In Leishmania, which has a whip-like structure at one end of the cell, binary fission occurs in any plane.
False 2: In Amoeba, which has a whip-like structure at one end of the cell, binary fission occurs in a definite orientation.

True Statement: Plasmodium, the malarial parasite, divides into many daughter cells simultaneously by multiple fission.
False 1: Plasmodium, the malarial parasite, divides into two daughter cells by binary fission.
False 2: Leishmania, the kala-azar parasite, divides into many daughter cells simultaneously by multiple fission.

True Statement: Yeast reproduces by putting out small buds that separate and grow further.
False 1: Yeast reproduces by binary fission into two equal halves.
False 2: Hydra reproduces by putting out small buds that separate and grow further.

True Statement: Spirogyra simply breaks up into smaller pieces upon maturation; these fragments grow into new individuals in a process called fragmentation.
False 1: Hydra simply breaks up into smaller pieces upon maturation; these fragments grow into new individuals in a process called fragmentation.
False 2: Spirogyra divides into two equal halves upon maturation in a process called fragmentation.

True Statement: Simple animals like Hydra and Planaria can be cut into any number of pieces and each piece grows into a complete organism; this is called regeneration.
False 1: Simple animals like Hydra and Planaria can be cut into any number of pieces but none of the pieces grows into a complete organism; this is called regeneration.
False 2: Simple organisms like Spirogyra and Amoeba can be cut into any number of pieces and each piece grows into a complete organism; this is called regeneration.

True Statement: Regeneration is carried out by specialised cells that proliferate and make large numbers of cells, which then differentiate into various cell types and tissues.
False 1: Regeneration is carried out by all body cells equally, which simultaneously differentiate into various cell types and tissues.

True Statement: Regeneration is not the same as reproduction since most organisms would not normally depend on being cut up to be able to reproduce.
False 1: Regeneration is the same as reproduction since most organisms depend on being cut up to reproduce.

True Statement: In Hydra, a bud develops as an outgrowth due to repeated cell division at one specific site, matures into a tiny individual, and detaches to become a new independent individual.
False 1: In Hydra, a bud develops as an inward growth due to repeated cell division at one specific site, matures into a tiny individual, and detaches to become a new independent individual.
False 2: In Planaria, a bud develops as an outgrowth due to repeated cell division at one specific site, matures into a tiny individual, and detaches to become a new independent individual.

True Statement: In many plants, parts like the root, stem and leaves can develop into new plants under appropriate conditions; this is vegetative propagation.
False 1: In all animals, parts like the root, stem and leaves can develop into new plants under appropriate conditions; this is vegetative propagation.

True Statement: Plants raised by vegetative propagation can bear flowers and fruits earlier than those produced from seeds.
False 1: Plants raised by vegetative propagation bear flowers and fruits later than those produced from seeds.

True Statement: Vegetative propagation makes possible the propagation of plants like banana, orange, rose and jasmine that have lost the capacity to produce seeds.
False 1: Vegetative propagation makes possible the propagation of plants like wheat, rice and maize that have lost the capacity to produce seeds.

True Statement: All plants produced by vegetative propagation are genetically similar enough to the parent plant to have all its characteristics.
False 1: All plants produced by vegetative propagation are genetically different from the parent plant and develop new characteristics.

True Statement: Buds produced in the notches along the leaf margin of Bryophyllum fall on soil and develop into new plants.
False 1: Buds produced in the notches along the leaf margin of Spirogyra fall on soil and develop into new plants.
False 2: Buds produced at the stem nodes of Bryophyllum fall on soil and develop into new plants.

True Statement: In spore formation, sporangia contain spores that can develop into new Rhizopus individuals; spores are covered by thick walls that protect them until they encounter a moist surface.
False 1: In spore formation, sporangia contain spores that can develop into new Rhizopus individuals; spores have thin walls that make them vulnerable until they encounter a moist surface.

True Statement: All modes of reproduction that create new generations from a single individual are known as asexual reproduction.
False 1: All modes of reproduction that create new generations from a single individual are known as sexual reproduction.

True Statement: The sexual mode of reproduction incorporates a process of combining DNA from two different individuals during reproduction, creating new combinations of variants.
False 1: The sexual mode of reproduction incorporates a process of copying DNA from a single individual during reproduction, creating exact duplicates.

True Statement: To keep the chromosome number constant across generations, special germ-cells contain only half the number of chromosomes compared to non-reproductive body cells; this is achieved by meiosis.
False 1: To keep the chromosome number constant across generations, special germ-cells contain double the number of chromosomes compared to non-reproductive body cells; this is achieved by mitosis.

True Statement: The motile germ-cell is called the male gamete and the germ-cell containing stored food is called the female gamete.
False 1: The motile germ-cell is called the female gamete and the germ-cell containing stored food is called the male gamete.

True Statement: Stamen is the male reproductive part of a flower and it produces pollen grains that are yellowish in colour.
False 1: Pistil is the male reproductive part of a flower and it produces pollen grains that are yellowish in colour.
False 2: Stamen is the female reproductive part of a flower and it produces pollen grains that are yellowish in colour.

True Statement: Pistil is the female reproductive part of a flower, made of three parts: the ovary (swollen bottom), style (middle elongated part) and stigma (terminal part which may be sticky).
False 1: Pistil is the female reproductive part of a flower, made of three parts: the stigma (swollen bottom), style (middle elongated part) and ovary (terminal part which may be sticky).
False 2: Stamen is the female reproductive part of a flower, made of three parts: the ovary, style and stigma.

True Statement: The ovary contains ovules and each ovule has an egg cell.
False 1: The stigma contains ovules and each ovule has an egg cell.
False 2: The ovary contains pollen grains and each pollen grain has an egg cell.

True Statement: If pollen is transferred within the same flower, it is called self-pollination; if transferred from one flower to another, it is called cross-pollination.
False 1: If pollen is transferred within the same flower, it is called cross-pollination; if transferred from one flower to another, it is called self-pollination.

True Statement: After the pollen lands on the stigma, a tube grows out of the pollen grain and travels through the style to reach the ovary.
False 1: After the pollen lands on the stigma, a tube grows out of the ovary and travels through the style to reach the pollen grain.

True Statement: After fertilisation, the zygote divides to form an embryo within the ovule; the ovule develops a tough coat and is gradually converted into a seed.
False 1: After fertilisation, the zygote divides to form an embryo within the ovary; the ovary develops a tough coat and is gradually converted into a seed.

True Statement: The ovary grows rapidly and ripens to form a fruit; the seed contains the future plant or embryo which develops into a seedling under appropriate conditions (germination).
False 1: The ovule grows rapidly and ripens to form a fruit; the seed contains the future plant or embryo which develops into a seedling under appropriate conditions (germination).

True Statement: The testes are located outside the abdominal cavity in the scrotum because sperm formation requires a lower temperature than the normal body temperature.
False 1: The testes are located inside the abdominal cavity because sperm formation requires a higher temperature than the normal body temperature.

True Statement: Testosterone regulates the formation of sperms and brings about changes in appearance seen in boys at puberty.
False 1: Oestrogen regulates the formation of sperms and brings about changes in appearance seen in boys at puberty.

True Statement: Sperms are delivered through the vas deferens which unites with a tube from the urinary bladder to form the urethra — a common passage for both sperms and urine.
False 1: Sperms are delivered through the fallopian tube which unites with a tube from the urinary bladder to form the urethra — a common passage for both sperms and urine.

True Statement: Glands like the prostate and seminal vesicles add secretions to provide fluid that makes sperm transport easier and provides nutrition to the sperms.
False 1: Glands like the prostate and seminal vesicles remove fluid from the sperms to make their transport easier.

True Statement: Sperms are tiny bodies that consist mainly of genetic material and a long tail that helps them move towards the female germ-cell.
False 1: Sperms are tiny bodies that consist mainly of stored food and a long tail that helps them move towards the female germ-cell.

True Statement: One egg is produced every month by one of the ovaries and is carried through a thin oviduct or fallopian tube to the uterus.
False 1: Two eggs are produced every month by one of the ovaries and are carried through a thin oviduct or fallopian tube to the uterus.

True Statement: The two oviducts unite into an elastic bag-like structure known as the uterus, which opens into the vagina through the cervix.
False 1: The two oviducts unite into an elastic bag-like structure known as the ovary, which opens into the vagina through the cervix.
False 2: The two oviducts unite into an elastic bag-like structure known as the uterus, which opens into the vagina through the fallopian tube.

True Statement: Fertilisation occurs in the oviduct; the fertilised egg (zygote) starts dividing to form an embryo which is implanted in the lining of the uterus.
False 1: Fertilisation occurs in the uterus; the fertilised egg (zygote) starts dividing to form an embryo which is implanted in the lining of the oviduct.

True Statement: The embryo gets nutrition from the mother's blood with the help of a special tissue called the placenta, which contains villi on the embryo's side.
False 1: The embryo gets nutrition from the mother's blood with the help of a special tissue called the amnion, which contains villi on the embryo's side.

True Statement: The development of the child inside the mother's body takes approximately nine months.
False 1: The development of the child inside the mother's body takes approximately six months.

True Statement: If the egg is not fertilised, it lives for about one day; the uterine lining breaks down and comes out through the vagina as blood and mucus — this is menstruation.
False 1: If the egg is not fertilised, it lives for about one week; the uterine lining thickens further and comes out through the vagina as blood and mucus — this is menstruation.

True Statement: Menstruation usually lasts for about two to eight days.
False 1: Menstruation usually lasts for about two to eight weeks.

True Statement: Bacterial sexually transmitted infections include gonorrhoea and syphilis; viral infections include warts and HIV-AIDS.
False 1: Bacterial sexually transmitted infections include warts and HIV-AIDS; viral infections include gonorrhoea and syphilis.

True Statement: Using a condom for the penis during sex helps to prevent transmission of many sexually transmitted infections.
False 1: Using a condom for the penis during sex provides no protection against sexually transmitted infections.

True Statement: Oral contraceptive pills work by changing the hormonal balance of the body so that eggs are not released and fertilisation cannot occur.
False 1: Oral contraceptive pills work by creating a mechanical barrier so that sperm does not reach the egg.

True Statement: A copper-T is placed in the uterus to prevent pregnancy.
False 1: A copper-T is placed in the fallopian tube to prevent pregnancy.

True Statement: If the vas deferens in the male is blocked, sperm transfer will be prevented; if the fallopian tube in the female is blocked, the egg will not reach the uterus — in both cases fertilisation will not take place.
False 1: If the vas deferens in the male is blocked, urine flow will be prevented; if the fallopian tube in the female is blocked, hormones will not reach the uterus — in both cases fertilisation will not take place.
